newsitem.title: SWEDEN: EU's de Silguy says ERM prerequisite for EMU.
newsitem.headline: EU's de Silguy says ERM prerequisite for EMU.

text.p: Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy said on Friday that an EU member should participate in the exchange rate mechanism (ERM) before joining the economic and monetary union (EMU).

"An EU country cannot have devalued its currency in relation to another EU country for two years before entering EMU," de Silguy, responsible for economic, financial and monetary affairs told reporters at an EMU seminar.

"A country should also have participated in ERM before entering EMU. This is what most EU countries think," he said, but added that it was up to heads of state to decide the issue at the beginning of 1998.
"I can naturally not say what they will decide," he said.
Sweden has repeatedly said that a stable currency is the key issue for EMU membership and not necessarily ERM participation.
Swedish Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said that the issue was one on which he and de Silguy differed but they did not discuss it at Friday's talks.
"We have had some different opinions about, for example, the currency exchange rate criteria," Asbrink told a news conference earlier.
He said that he was aware that Sweden held a minority view but it was nevertheless impossible to predict the outcome when members are evaluated in the spring of 1998.
"That is up to the 15 member countries' leaders," Asbrink said.
Sweden's minority Social Democratic government has said that the party's congress will decide whether to seek EMU membership in the autumn of 1997, with a parliamentary vote expected to follow.
